title: This Seabird Spits Stinking Oil Three Meters to Stop Attackers

scenes.text: This seabird's weapon comes out of its mouth.
It's a northern fulmar. When a predator comes close, it spits stomach oil up to about three meters.
The oil stinks and it clings. On a bird of prey, it can coat the feathers, and that can be deadly.
Even chicks can do it, from a very young age.
The oil isn't only a weapon. It's energy-rich food for chicks, and for adults on long flights.
On Scotland's St Kilda, islanders even burned it as candles. The name fulmar means foul gull.

description:
A northern fulmar can spit stinking stomach oil about three meters at predators.
It is also food for chicks and was once burned as candles on St Kilda.
Would you walk near a fulmar nest?
first_comment: Spit, slime or spray: which animal defence would you hate to face?
